                                                 OilGuard AI
Digital Twin for Oil Field Safety Monitoring

OpenEgiz Digital Mine Competition

Team: team-089 | Solo participant

A fictional oil field inspired by western Kazakhstan.




                                                               OilGuard AI | 1

[страница 2]
1. The Problem
Oil production equipment operates under changing pressure, temperature and vibration.

Abnormal measurements can indicate potential equipment failures and safety risks.

OilGuard AI demonstrates how a digital twin can help operators recognize dangerous conditions earlier.




                                                                                                         OilGuard AI | 2

[страница 3]
2. Digital Twin Architecture
The simulated oil field contains one parent digital twin and three production well twins.

Parent: oilfield-01

Wells: WELL-01, WELL-02 and WELL-03

Each well has pressure, temperature, vibration and operational status features.

Telemetry messages are prepared in the Eclipse Ditto protocol format for OpenEgiz integration.




                                                                                                 OilGuard AI | 3

[страница 4]
3. Safety Detection Algorithm
The Python simulator generates 360 telemetry records across 120 simulated minutes.

A record is classified as DANGER if at least one illustrative threshold is exceeded:

Pressure > 80 bar

Temperature > 90 degrees Celsius

Vibration > 7 mm/s

An abnormal event is introduced in WELL-02 during minutes 70 through 90.

These thresholds are demonstration assumptions, not certified industrial limits.




                                                                                       OilGuard AI | 4

[страница 5]
4. Simulation Results
360 total telemetry records | 3 wells | 21 DANGER records




                                                            OilGuard AI | 5

[страница 6]
5. Results and Next Steps
Verified locally: dataset generation, safety status detection, pressure chart, four twin definitions and MQTT dry-run
messages.

Not yet verified: live OpenEgiz deployment, Grafana dashboard and interactive What-if controls.

Next steps: connect the simulator to a running OpenEgiz Stand, visualize live telemetry and add operator-controlled
scenarios.

The model uses synthetic data and is not intended for real industrial safety decisions.
